posts.title: So, what Do people want?
posts.text: - A return of the 'Fun At The...' Minifigure sets - to give a wider variety of figures available for more specific activities and environments (e.g. fun at the ski lodge, fun at the wedding, fun at the water park, fund at the skating rink)... - Lettering bricks - Square tiles with a right angle and opposite curve that complement the existing rounded tiles - Useful printed parts in modular sets (e.g. Travel posters or a World map for a travel agency) - World Flags like in Set 242 'International Flags' - these can be based on World Cup participating teams to avoid seemingly favouring particular nations above others - Safari sets in City (and other wildlife sets) - not released in one sole wave never to be seen again though, give us a new one each wave and within a couple of years we'll have all the main missing animals (giraffe, hippo + baby, zebra, rhino, gazelle, meerkat, hyena...) - Return of the Adventurers (or at least a tribute set using all the original hieroglyphic pieces - don't you even dare try doing it with stickers, Lego) - Stop making Lego less fun in feeling that it needs to be bought only at certain times to get value for money (e.g. when a particular GWP is available or double points). I just want to buy it throughout the year and not feel I'm missing out and have to wait for a better deal - it's taking all the enjoyment from being a Lego hobbyist these days. - More animals in CMF series (including baby versions of bigger animals) - More variety with trains - don't just release big train sets but smaller sets to allow collectors to buy additional carriages, plus other train-related items like bridges, signals, track that can incline. Otherwise if you must release large sets, please base them in more interesting locations like an Andean or Outback Train and include animals (e.g. llamas or kangaroos)... - Stop cheapening sets with stickers (Yuck! ) - Less of the sets increasing in size all the times and at an equally unaffordable cost (storage space is a big issue for long-term fans). For example, sets like the gorilla set didn't need the enormous helicopter and the Venetian Neighbourhood didn't need a non-Lego piano piece, thus increasing the price even more. Stop being so unpleasantly greedy Lego - you have lost my respect as a company and I spend far less than nowadays that I did before as a result. It feels like you only cater for the Johnny-come-lately fans these days.

posts.title: Modular Building Sets - Rumours and Discussion
posts.text: I'm not disappointed by a single base plate modular. It keeps costs down and it doesn't take up a lot of space. Assembly Square was three buildings, which was fine, as they all kept to scale with the other modulars. Natural History Museum was a little disappointing as it was smaller than you'd expect for a museum, especially compared to the other modulars. It should have been a lot taller to scale properly. Of course, doing that would mean a much higher price for little additional value. But it's for that reason that I'm very happy with a single baseplate modular as they then have the budget to make a really good set, rather than risk it getting too diluted over the extra space.

posts.title: Lego Blockly: Graphical Common Programming Environment Web App (Using Intuitive Blockly) for All Lego Robotic Platforms.
posts.text: @Bliss Another idea just popped in there :D The non-LEGO interface "ecosystem" of LEGO Blockly (to connect to selected LEGO interfaces, e.g., Int.A, PF, Cubes) consists of ESP32 based microcontrollers. How about making a "generic" LEGO Blockly ESP32 based interface, e.g., using the beloved WROOM 32 DevKit 1 boards? 4 or more inputs (GPIOs), just A/D conversion (no Wifi = multiplexed ADC1+2 available). 4 or more inputs - just digital. 6 or more outputs. Reasoning: TLG only made "some" types of sensors. They are generally rather bulky, particularly the later generations (need to be for ruggedness and data handling), and are expensive. Furthermore, most LEGO interfaces except Int.B have max. 3 inputs and outputs. There are myriads of dead cheap sensors out there, which are or can be made ESP32 compatible With the super-small H bridge modules, even motors can be attached; e.g. 4.5V LEGO motors (using 5V USB power supply) When using C3's or the like, they could be placed anywhere (where there is USB power) and serve as "remote sensors". In this case the number of GPIOs is restricted, of course. Optionally (and not really needed) you could even add OLED displays to such generic ESP32 servers, and LEGO Blockly would do the text output ... Just an idea ... Best Thorsten

But in general I just have zero faith in adaptations, I just treat them as someone else's interpretations of characters. Sometimes an actual quality and faithful adaptation will come along, but it's very rare. I guess that sounds like a downer, but I rather offer my own interpretation of these characters as I work on breaking into comics.

posts.title: [Help for MOC] Lego City Hyper Tower (inspired by Lego City Tower 60473)
posts.text: Hello, When the LEGO City Tower came out, I really liked the Idea, but always felt there was too less of everything. So I was thinking about how far one could take that. For sure this isn't a typical set which fits in a big organized AFOL City. I see it more as a standalone crazy city diorama or a really fun play set. I would really like to build the set by myself, but I'm lacking the time to design this several thousand pieces set. I've got a really detailed concept and have built a very rough model in studio2.0 as a proof of concept and size. The only limit I've set for this set is width of below 75 studs. So my question is, is anyone crazy enough to join me or take over this project? My idea adds some basic unspectacular things as well as some insane plot twists. Ground floor The center this time isn't the subway but a little museum. This exhibits at least a mid sized dinosaur (Raptor or Small T Rex), a historic figure like a Knight or Mummy, something worthy behind a laser grid like a diamond or so. On its right hand there is a 8 studs wide garage for a fire engine. But this time a real one, not a small car. Still 6 studs wide but with an extendable ladder, a real hose, and big bay for some tools. Seats two. Still compact but full of features. Next to it a police station. Also with a 8 Studs wide garage but also a little Office and jail next to it, accessible from the side. The police car would still be racecar like, 6 Studs, but with a backseat for the villain. The jail has some kind of breakout funktion, like exploding a wall with dynamite or so. The office has a computer, some donuts. On the left side of the museum there's a small car workshop / tuning garage. Theres a racecar in an equal kind like the police car, features a backseat or more like a trunk. This could be taken for races or maybe a robber steals it to escape. The tuning workshop can make the racecars off-road cars with bigger wheels or make them flying cars by replacing wheels with impellers. The building ends here, but left to it there's now real railroad track instead of a subway. With a small 2-3 studs platform for passengers to board the train. Right above the railroads there is a large crane. It's legs are directly left and right from the railroad, so the train passes through it. Directly left from the crane and railroad there is a small parallel wharf where container ship can dock. There's also a lifebuoy and someone with a fishing rod, but I guess only a shark and maybe an octopuses is included in this set so stay cautious. I've also heard rumors there's a treasure chest somewhere in the sea. The set features unique containers system with 6x12 Studs Containers with roof sloped to the sides. Some are for different cargo, some are for passengers (at least 6 per container). The crane can load these containers to the train, cargo ship and a container truck. The train consists of two power cars with one aerodynamical driver cabin on each, end and each can load a container which sits flush on it with the same sloped roofline. This way it can be used as a passenger or cargo train. The cargo ship is rather compact and 12 studs wide but loads 2 or 3 containers. It features small cabin with at least bed and a place to cook, likely more, as well as a small command bridge for 2. Since the 12 wide containers have to stand on top the 12 wide ship, below the containers theres are hatches which open up an additional cargo hold inside the ship. As if that isn't enough, it can also slide out a ramp for cars and act as a small ferry too. It also has a small crane to unload things on its own. There is also little submarine seating one, which also is 6x12 in size and can be loaded like a container to the truck, train and in every case the ship, transforming it into a research ship. The cargo truck can not only load one container but also has a winch behind the cabin and a ramp, which also makes it a flatbed tow truck. I've also tried it making look like a bus when loadi

posts.text: I think they’ll continue to try and strike a balance between the Mario Kart and platformer games the way they’ve done for this first wave. I know the Course Builder system was wholly dedicated to Mario Kart for a bit but the advantage of doing everything in System scale is how many more karts and characters can be squeezed into sets now. I know I’ve already said this before but 4+ aside, I genuinely love how all of the playsets for January have some real love and effort put into them. This could have very much become a theme where they banked on the minifigures compensating for the builds but I’m so happy that isn’t the case. It makes me incredibly optimistic for the future of this theme. And yeah, sign me up for a playscale Odyssey. It could almost be done in full minifigure scale without even needing a large price point. Anything from the Galaxy games would own my heart too, and an Airship sounds like a no-brainer for next summer’s non-D2C flagship set.

posts.text: Luke Starkiller could potentially be one of the coolest Star Wars minifigures we’ve seen in a really long time! I’m very excited to see the packaging too. Awesome package art goes such a long way in the appeal of a set for me. I really, really hope that the minifigures we get are damn good. Whether or not I get Duel on Mustafar will wholly depend on if Anakin and Obi-Wan are fully updated rather than being half-baked minor improvements on their 2020 versions. The leakers have been very quiet on the quality of the minifigures themselves, fingers crossed Lego had a big budget to work with next year. Anakin will (supposedly) have arm-printing. I asked one of the leakers on the Brick Tap Discord a few weeks back Alas I share your delusion comrade. Now we know how it felt to be Yoda when he was faced with the visions from the Force Priestesses. Realistically, I can see both BHP and Ewok Village being slated for 2028 rather than being cancelled entirely. However, I commend the geniuses who saw that the 50 year anniversary celebration of the franchise was coming and decided that, no, we actually need more Smart Play and Marvel crossover stuff rather than two sets that act as iconic representations of the movies they stem from that would have been perfect for a year like 2027. And seriously, have can a theme not have any playsets within the entire second half of a year? Has that ever happened before for playscale themes? Anyway, this feels like the calm before the storm of set images. I’m trying to keep my expectations modest but all the same, I can’t help feeling incredibly excited.

posts.title: What is your SigFig?
posts.text: Huh? SigFigs??? Folks. I am struggling with teaching the impact of significant figures on a result for decades (and it doesn't get any better), just to find this 23-page thread ... My favorite sig fig is 2. I am an experimentalist. So whatever I do - results have errors. Given the appropriate "scaling" is applied, e.g., nm for wavelength in the visible range, more than 2 decimals is - fancy stuff. If you'd use 3 sig figs I'd seriously doubt your claim and tell you to show me your setup. There are ways ... When you measure a length with a ruler, you'll never be accurate to 0.01 mm ... So yes: 2 is my SigFig. (OK, I am kidding; it was a long day) Best Thorsten

posts.text: Seems to run fine! Now, when in BASIC mode, is there a need for the graphics window on the top right (the "turtle" window?). Which BASIC version are you emulating? posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: I've never actually watched Agatha. I just am not very invested in the character and witch stuff and musical aspects are not things that I tend to enjoy. But I have heard people liked it. Yeah Hawkeye was a fun show. It started the character assassination of the Daredevil cast, but taken by itself it's very good. If you have any interest in daredevil or any characters within his sphere, there is one scene in S1E4 that's pretty good (because Bernthal rewrote his dialogue) and you should stay far away from everything else in Born Again. It's almost comical how concretely it undoes all development and even major plot points. It essentially replaces S3 of the netflix series, but because the netflix show became canon, if you watch it in order every character just undoes all their development to repeat S3 with worse writing. I think my favorite aspects of it are that S3 has a big focus on Matt learning that he and daredevil must coexist and he can't try to be just one or the other, and needs to let his friends be in his life, that ends with him finding his mom- and then Born Again has him deny who he is again, he's cut off from his friends, and his mom gets mentioned once throughout the first season (I dunno if she was in the second I couldn't watch it). There's also a major plot in season 3 about FBI Agent Nadeem who quickly becomes a fan favorite, and is the one ultimately responsible for putting Fisk away for good. Born Again casually mentions that the reason Fisk is out and able to run for mayor is because Nadeem was corrupt or something. In the netflix series the man literally sacrifices his life to ensure his testimony is admissible, and he's brushed aside without a second thought in Born Again. As for vision quest: No, that's fair. Hawkeye is a lot of fun. My more concrete ranking than the earlier one: 1. Loki: Genuinely an amazing show. The last two episodes of the series deserved Emmys and are legitimate contenders for the best things the MCU has ever made. 2. Vison Quest: Not even done yet and I know it deserves this spot. Even if it drops the ball in the latter half, it's so far ahead of everything else that it'd stay in #2. Large Gap 3. Hawkeye: This is about what I'd expect of an MCU show if it'd been produced back during the MCU's heyday. It's nothing super deep, but it's fun. Loses a few points for what it did to Kingpin. 4. Moon Knight: A good show that's a terrible adaption of the titular character. But that just goes to show that it was a solid show, if it butchered the character and still ends up towards the top of the list. 5. Wandavision: A very unique and interesting premise that justified the idea of the MCU branching into miniseries. It dropped the ball in the latter half- Wanda essentially just getting away with her crimes, Hayward going from pretty reasonable to trying to shoot children, the finale just becoming "punch the bad guys"- but it really swung for the fences and while it wasn't a home run, it at least got somebody on the bases. Large Gap 6. What If: I admittedly stopped partway through season 2 and I'm sure my ranking would be lower if I finished it. It has two good episodes- the Strange and Ultron ones. 7. TFATWS: John is the saving grace of an otherwise terrible show. It's truly impressive that most people were on board with or at least apathetic to Samcap after Endgame, and a show dedicated to giving him the title made people turn against him. 8. Born Again: At the end of the day, Charlie Cox, Jon Bernthal, and Vincent D'nofrio deliver performances as good as ever. But the writing is monumentally terrible, as if they're actively undoing the netflix series. Bernthal was wise enough to limit his involvement and rewrite his dialogue, but he should have rejected it like he's reported to have initially done. Final gap 9. She-Hulk: Everything wrong with modern marvel. 10. Secret Invasion: This one stings the most because I was fully on board with this show. I thought this was going to be the best MCU

posts.title: Bricklink Designer Program Trains Sets | 2024 & Beyond
posts.text: As said, nose and cab got their PUp LED "lighting". And I can gladly put aside the PUp app/my cellphone and use my Dell laptop and/or a PUp remote to control the F7. You may or may not have heard of "LEGO Blockly" a graphical programming language developed by EB member @Bliss. I threw together the LEGO Blockly program this afternoon - it is so easy to do: All this does is increase the speed (not the power) of the train in 5% steps (scale 0-90%), allowing the PID algorithm in the hub firmware to regulate power so that speed is held constant. Max speed is 90%; 100% = losing the PID control almost entirely. At 5% speed the locomotive crawls smoothly and slowly and constant speed. You may ask: What's new? TLG PoweredUp app does something similar? Well, here we go: I really hate to use a cell phone for train control. I like either my laptop or a remote to do so. Directly connecting the PUp remote to a City hub is a no-go, as motors like a PUp L are treated badly by the remote: They just go full forward or full reverse when you press the + or - button. Only a dumb PUp motor, e.g., the train motor gets the + = increase power by some percentage and vice versa. The blocks in the PUp app were not that intuitive to me; once I used it for a bit it got better, but after a couple of months not using it, I neede to start over. I come from programming using text lines. BASIC, PASCAL, some C++. LEGO Blockly is entirely different; you just click blocks together. But still, I can literally "read" the string of blocks, see the loops etc. LEGO Blockly, in contrast to its name, features mostly non-blocking elements - the "execute and forget" type. It can do multi-tasking (Yes, PoweredUp as well but) ... There are some interactive elements, but I really hardly need any, when using remotes. So as usually: Just sign up the remote and the hub (one mouse click) and done. Again, you may ask: What's new? Well, here comes the kicker: With just another mouse click, I can connect to an Interface A or B, an RCX, Cybermaster, NXT, WeDo1/2, PF, Dimension Toypad, a USB serial tower (VLL as well as IR), and to Circuit Cubes. Every time identical blocks, with sometimes different features, of course; PF does not have PID control, etc. Oh: No installation necessary, none whatsoever. It runs in a browser or as stand-alone application on your computer. Which is just another mouse click. There is even more to come - this is really incredible. Just take a look, if you have not yet: Best Thorsten

posts.title: [MOC] Grundtvigskirken
posts.text: My latest model is Grundtvigskirken in Copenhagen, presented with lifestyle images similar to the official LEGO images of sets like Notre Dame and Sagrada Familia The church was finished in 1940 and designed by Danish architect P.V. Jensen Klint. See all pictures of my model in this Flickr album. The model uses around 2000 masonry bricks as well as palisade bricks for the vertical lines and profile bricks for the horizontal lines near the roof. There is a built-in LED light strip which reveals that the windows are built from 1x1 dark transparent bricks to mimic the true glass pattern. Some details: With a module size of 8 studs between the outside pillars, the entire roof is offset by half a stud to center the top of the roof correctly. Sketches and plans of the church, including rulers, was available online. Along with aerial photos and my own pictures from the church, it was possible to create a very accurate model with all proportions true to the original. Finally some reference pictures: The iconic facade: The church and the surroundings: I hope you enjoyed the presentation. Do leave a comment. Thanks. Esben

posts.text: Fast forward to May of 2020. This was shortly after moving to another location (was very fun during first Covid lockdown) when my minifigures were due for some cleaning: New highlights were definitely the whole 20th anniversary lineup:

posts.title: Bricklink Designer Program Trains Sets | 2024 & Beyond
posts.text: I'd be interested to see somebody who's built Tony Sava's EMD F7 get a side-by-side with the BDP set - similar designs of the same locomotive, but a few major distinctions between the two (particularly the cab windows).

posts.title: [MOC] UT/F-150 Raptor Shuttle
posts.text: Love the pictures in all sorts of environments. Something to be said for simple, rugged, and dependable. The design appears to mimic those qualities as well.

posts.title: [MOC] Surface Explorer
posts.text: Small, but it looks like a fun ride. This would be a perfect polybag set.

posts.title: Imperial Airship
posts.text: Incredible ship. The Dieselpunk feel is quite evident, along with some Mediterranean and Middle Eastern vibes. From the prow to the engines, it has a classic pre-dreadnought lines. The anchor chain holes almost make me think of eyes. Great work.

posts.title: Building Bellona: a 74-gun WIP
posts.text: Amazing work and attention to the shaping. I like how you're starting out with the line drawings and working from there in lieu of on the computer. Old school rules!

posts.title: Would you trust AI to book your estimates?
posts.text: I've been testing AI phone answering for my brother's landscaping company. Getting it to answer questions is one thing, but letting it put appointments on the calendar is another. There are jobs we don't take, and the last thing I want is an estimate booked for something we don't even do. Would you let AI book estimates, or would you rather have it take the information and call the customer back?

posts.title: How do you monitor snow storms?
posts.text: We're prepping for this years snow season and need some way to best track storms and expected snowfall for our sites. How does everyone do this? We have about 20 trucks/plows across a large metro and previous years our ex manager would do it all checking weather. Many times he'd be wildly wrong. Is this just the norm, check weather.com and see whats expected in the area or is there a better way to track storms? Also is there anything people use afterwards for an after action report... How do you monitor snow storms?

posts.title: Made my first 10k
posts.text: Hey y'all, Hit a milestone and wanted to share it with y'all. 10k in almost all lawn mowing. I've done some cleanups, etc., but only for current clients, and only a handful of times. My marketing was about 2 grand or so and it was all print media( Door hangers and postcards); 5 of my clients were from last season.
